name: Brave farbling (Brave Shields 'Fingerprinting defenses 2.0' / fingerprint randomization); the randomization-per-session-per-eTLD+1 model, contrasted with Tor's uniformity model
kind: Browser feature, shipped in a Chromium fork. Not a standard and not an extractor. The underlying idea — per-origin-per-session deterministic noise seeded from a session key — is the transferable artifact.
maturity: Production since 2020 and continuously revised (defenses 1.0 through 2.0 and beyond). The mechanism is stable; the target list and the noise magnitudes are not.
license: MPL 2.0 (Brave's own code) over BSD-3 Chromium. Permits use. The relevant question for this project is not licensing but whether the Chromium base is acceptable at all, given the project drives Firefox.
keeps_and_discards: Not an extraction approach and it discards no DOM content. It perturbs the OUTPUT of a bounded set of semi-identifying APIs: canvas readback (getImageData / toDataURL pixel-level noise), Web Audio (a randomized fudge factor applied to the audio buffer), WebGL parameters, plugin and font enumeration, and several navigator surfaces. The noise is deterministic given (session seed, eTLD+1), so it is stable within a site within a session and different across sites and across sessions. At Aggressive shields level additional APIs are blocked outright rather than farbled, which does remove capability.
structure_preserved: Completely — the DOM, its nesting, ordering, tabular relations and shadow boundaries are untouched. Farbling operates strictly at the API-return-value layer. Open shadow roots traverse normally; closed roots do not; Brave adds no shadow access. The single content-relevant exception is a page that renders text or structure INTO a canvas and reads it back, where farbled pixels can corrupt the read; that is a narrow class (OCR-in-page, canvas-based charting, some captcha implementations).
interactive_elements: Untouched. Controls remain ordinary DOM nodes and scripts run normally at Standard shields. At Aggressive, blocked APIs can break control initialisation, producing markup that looks interactive and is not — the same silent divergence Tor's Safer level produces, by a different route.
interactive_state_fidelity: Fully preserved at Standard shields, for the same reason as Firefox RFP: all page scripts execute, so disabled / checked / selected / aria-expanded reflect real post-script state, and the accessibility tree is untouched. Farbling costs zero tokens and zero state fidelity in extraction terms. At Aggressive shields, script initialisation failures can leave ARIA state frozen at parse-time values with no error raised, which is a real (if narrow) state-fidelity hazard. [uncertain] No published measurement of ARIA-state divergence under Aggressive shields exists.
layout_awareness: Does not read page geometry and, unlike Firefox letterboxing and Tor, does not quantise the viewport either. This is farbling's cleanest property relative to this project: it is the one major fingerprinting defense that leaves the geometry peripheral entirely alone. Font-enumeration farbling can shift text metrics on pages relying on unusual fonts, which is a second-order layout effect, but there is no viewport rounding and no forced margins.
javascript_required: Scripts always run at Standard shields; farbling is a value-substitution layer inside script execution, not a script suppressor. Telemetry therefore fires exactly as unhardened. Brave's ad/tracker blocking (a separate Shields component, effectively an EasyList-family blocker) is what suppresses requests, and that is the component that would carry a measured fidelity cost comparable to the local block_trackers arm — not farbling itself. Keeping those two components conceptually separate is essential; they are usually conflated.
evaluation_method: Brave evaluates by adversary argument plus internal web-compat testing, publishing rationale in its privacy-updates blog series rather than in peer-reviewed benchmarks. External evaluation comes from academic attacks on canvas-fingerprinting defenses and from fuzzy-matching studies that test whether randomized fingerprints re-link. There is no extraction-fidelity evaluation of farbling by anyone.
corpus_size_and_origins: No fixed corpus, for either breakage or effectiveness. Breakage evidence is the brave-browser GitHub issue queue — an unbounded, self-selected sample of complaints (the audio-farbling distortion report on multi-voice Web Audio synthesis is a representative example). Academic attacks use their own small purpose-built page sets. Nothing is frozen; no number about farbling has a stable denominator.
reported_precision_recall: Not applicable in extraction terms. The security-relevant published figure is the residual re-identification rate under fuzzy matching, and the direction of that evidence is unfavourable to farbling: reported per-attribute deviations from the unfarbled fingerprint are extremely small at Standard level (figures on the order of 1e-6 relative difference circulate in third-party analyses), which is small enough that fuzzy or threshold matching can still cluster sessions. Treat any single quoted deviation figure as unreliable — it is measurement-methodology-dependent and not independently replicated. [uncertain]
independent_oracle: Yes, and it is genuinely adversarial: academic work on attacking canvas-fingerprinting defenses (including WWW-venue analyses of randomization defenses) does not share Brave's assumptions and tests the property Brave claims. That is a stronger independent oracle than exists for Tor's or Firefox's uniformity claims, and its verdict is qualified rather than clean — randomization is detectable and partially defeatable by averaging or fuzzy matching.
evidence_independence: Design rationale and most effectiveness claims are first-party Brave. The negative results are third-party academic. Breakage evidence is crowd-sourced. There is no vendor-neutral comparison of farbling against uniformity on a common corpus.
page_archetype_coverage: No published per-archetype figures. Mechanism-derived expectation: article, forum, documentation and listing pages are unaffected because they do not read canvas or audio; product and service pages that use canvas-rendered charts, canvas-based image editors, WebGL viewers, or audio-fingerprint-gated login flows are where farbling can change or break content. This is the narrowest archetype exposure of any defense in this set. [uncertain]
script_and_locale_behaviour: Better than RFP on this axis, because Brave does not force locale or timezone at Standard shields, so pages do not switch served language. Font-enumeration farbling can perturb fallback selection for CJK and Indic scripts and therefore shift text metrics and line-breaking, but the text content itself is unchanged. A text-only fold is script-invariant under farbling; a metrics-reading one is not.
leaks_outward: Reduces the linkability of the machine across origins without reducing what any single origin observes about the visit. Network-layer disclosure is unchanged unless Shields' blocking component is also enabled. Against the local 3,082-requests-to-92-hosts figure, farbling alone changes nothing; the blocking component is what would move it, at the 10.49%-on-live-sites scale already measured.
mechanism_detectability: Detectable and, unlike some theoretical tells, detected in practice. The specific signal is that farbled output is statistically distinguishable from real output: canvas readbacks that differ across origins on the same machine within one session, or across sessions on the same origin, when the underlying hardware has not changed, are a positive fingerprint OF Brave. Commercial fingerprinting SDKs (FingerprintJS and its lineage) explicitly identify Brave as a browser, and 'Brave detected' is a routinely available signal in anti-bot scoring today; the noise is the tell. This is the central irony of randomization defenses and is the same class of failure as RFP's attribute set: withholding entropy is itself entropy. Brave's own framing — noise 'difficult to detect' — should be read as difficult to characterise per-value, not difficult to attribute to Brave. Critically for this project's stated tension: farbling does nothing about automation detection. It does not touch navigator.webdriver, does not affect CDP Runtime.enable tells, and is orthogonal to Marionette. Running the sensor in Brave would add a Brave tell on top of whatever automation tell already exists.
countermeasures: The shields level (Standard / Aggressive / Off) is the coarse dial, and per-site shields toggles are the fine one. For a capture pipeline the correct setting is Standard with the blocking component considered separately, because Aggressive trades real capability for marginal entropy reduction. There is no supported way to keep farbling while suppressing the Brave-ness signal.
measured_fidelity_cost: Unmeasured publicly and, for farbling proper, expected to be near zero against a null control on any page that does not read canvas or audio. The prediction to test against the local anchors: farbling should land indistinguishably from the 0.07% null-control fold-drift floor on a text corpus, while Brave's tracker-blocking component should land near the already-measured block_trackers figures (10.49% live, 0.16% saved). If a farbling arm measured materially above the null floor on text-only pages, that would indicate the blocking component was not actually held constant — which is the most likely experimental error in any Brave arm. [uncertain]
gate_state_at_capture: Farbling records nothing about gate state. Its effect on gate incidence is genuinely ambiguous and worth naming rather than assuming: Brave detection raises risk scores at some anti-bot vendors, while Brave's blocking component suppresses many consent-management scripts outright, which can prevent a consent interface from ever rendering. That second effect is a trap — a capture where the CMP script was blocked looks ungated but is not, and with roughly 67% of top sites presenting a consent interface it would silently and substantially bias a corpus toward apparent-ungated. Gate state must be recorded from observed evidence, not inferred from banner absence.
determinism: Deterministic by construction within a session and origin — the noise is seeded from (session key, eTLD+1), so repeated reads of the same canvas in the same session on the same site return identical farbled values. This is a genuinely good design property and is the single most transferable idea in the item.
determinism_across_versions: Poor. The farbled target list, the noise magnitudes, and the shields defaults have all changed across Brave releases, and the Chromium base moves underneath. Any measured value is version-scoped. Additionally, because the seed rotates per session by design, cross-session determinism is intentionally absent — which means anything that hashes a canvas read is non-reproducible across runs on purpose.
reproducibility: Content reproducibility is unaffected. Any artifact that captured canvas output would be irreproducible across sessions by design. Since this project's fold is text and structure, that limitation does not bite unless canvas content ever enters the trie.
failure_modes: Audible distortion in Web Audio synthesis (a filed, reproduced issue); corrupted canvas-rendered charts and image processing; broken canvas-based fingerprint gates that then deny access; at Aggressive shields, outright script failure on API-dependent applications; and elevated anti-bot risk from Brave detection.
failure_visibility: Split, with the dangerous half silent. Aggressive-shields script failures are usually loud (console errors, visibly missing UI). Farbled-canvas corruption is silent — the page renders something, it is just wrong. Blocked-CMP-looks-ungated is silent and biasing. Farbling itself, on a text page, fails invisibly because it does nothing.
scale_limits: Negligible cost; value substitution inside the renderer. Linear in pages. The blocking component carries the usual filter-list memory and match cost, which is separately bounded.
delta_cost_model: No delta model of its own, and — unlike Firefox letterboxing — no adverse interaction with one, because farbling never changes viewport or layout. A canvas that is re-read returns the same farbled value within a session, so it does not manufacture spurious change. This is farbling's best property for an O(delta) architecture: it is delta-neutral where letterboxing is delta-hostile.
reanchoring_stability: Neutral. Node identity is untouched — xpath, content hash and CDC boundaries all behave as unhardened, because the DOM is unhardened. No measured re-anchor effect and none expected.
adversarial_exposure: No help. Farbling preserves zero-width and tag characters, comments, JSON-LD, display:none nodes and off-screen content exactly as authored; it has no concept of concealment. Unlike letterboxing it also does not disturb the ground truth of viewport-based hiding, since the viewport is unchanged. Net: neutral rather than harmful, which is better than the uniformity-model defenses manage.
provenance_carrying: None at the representation level. One capture-envelope fact matters: whether Shields' blocking component was on, because that determines whether absent third-party content (including consent interfaces) was blocked or genuinely absent.
roundtrip_safety: Not applicable; no serialisation, no escaping policy, no text normalisation.
token_budget_and_ordering: No effect. No truncation, no ordering, no context policy.
representation_cost: Zero token delta on text pages. Non-zero only where blocked or farbled APIs change how much markup a page emits, which is a Shields-blocking effect rather than a farbling effect.
what_could_be_adopted: The mechanism itself is not adoptable — this project drives Firefox, and switching to a Chromium fork to gain farbling would trade a single navigator.webdriver tell for a Brave tell plus CDP-layer exposure, which is a strictly worse detectability position. What IS adoptable is the design principle, and it is the sharpest one in the privacy set: SEEDED, DETERMINISTIC, PER-SCOPE noise rather than per-call randomness. Anywhere this project needs a value that must not be stable across scopes but must be reproducible within one, the (scope key, session seed) construction gives both properties at once, and Brave demonstrates it working in production. The second adoptable finding is negative and load-bearing for the project's own hardening arms: farbling is the only defense in this set that is provably delta-neutral and geometry-neutral, which makes it the correct reference point for asking what a hardening arm SHOULD cost. If a Firefox hardening arm costs materially more than a farbling-equivalent would, the excess is attributable to viewport quantisation or request suppression, not to entropy reduction.

constraint_violation_ledger.verdict: Negative oracle only as a browser choice (rejected as a platform switch); the seeded-deterministic-noise construction is adoptable as-is as a design pattern, and the shields-blocking component is adoptable in the actuator layer only.
constraint_violation_ledger.structure_agnosticism: No conflict. Farbling applies no structural heuristic and names no region. Fully compatible. Note the blocking component IS a rule list and does classify network resources, though not page regions.
constraint_violation_ledger.no_layout_in_the_fold: No conflict, and uniquely clean: farbling neither reads nor perturbs geometry, and does not quantise the viewport. Strictly better than Firefox letterboxing and Tor on this constraint.
constraint_violation_ledger.o_delta: No conflict. Delta-neutral by construction — seeded noise is stable within a session, so re-reads produce no spurious change and no invalidation cascade.
constraint_violation_ledger.no_mocks: Compatible at Standard shields (real browser, all scripts run). Violated in spirit at Aggressive shields, where blocked APIs make the captured page a different artifact from the real one. Aggressive should be excluded from any measured path.
constraint_violation_ledger.closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed: Fully consistent. Brave provides no shadow-root access and no attachShadow interference. Closed roots stay closed.

governance_signal_handling: None from farbling. Brave as a product carries adjacent governance behaviour (Shields blocking, and Brave's own crawler identity for its search index) but the fingerprinting defense reads no robots.txt, has no AIPREF, Content Signals or ai.txt awareness, cannot participate in Web Bot Auth, and treats an HTTP 402 as an ordinary error response. Like RFP, it is compatible with Web Bot Auth in principle: declaring a signed agent identity at the protocol layer and withholding hardware entropy at the API layer are independent choices.
legal_basis_and_pii_posture: Under EDPB Guidelines 03/2026 the regulated act is collecting and persistently storing personal data from public sources; the browser's entropy posture does not bear on the lawful basis for that storage. Farbling retains no PII and adds none to the artifact. Its only relevance to the legitimate-interest balancing is data minimisation about the capture process rather than about the stored fold.
